grantsNothing: A measurement. It issues no verdict, opens no route, moves no byte and edits no script. Its output is a per-family finding a repair lane can be dispatched from, one writer per host.
question: SCAN01 and four independent verifiers disagree about whether COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN families ship hard-split route keys and route-key-only pages. Which is right, why, and which proven families carry the defect on their current bytes?
answerInOneLine: On current bytes 35 of 154 measured families (150 proven + 4 Rhode Island) carry at least one class a-d defect; 119 were inspected page by page and carry none. The verifiers are right about every family they named. SCAN01's committed sweep also lists all five, so the miss is not in SCAN01's instrument: it is that the sweep is a point-in-time worklist that was never joined to the proven state, plus two measurement gaps and one stale family described below.

method.principle: The verifiers' method, not SCAN01's. Every page of every fixture PDF is inflated through the repository's own content-stream walker (scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-pdf-anchor-capture.mjs: extractTextItems + groupIntoLines, the same inflater the builders use to prove their writes back), every drawn line is reconstructed in reading order with its x/y baseline, and the text is matched against the family's OWN route keys. No width band and no font metric is a criterion; widths are recorded for context only. pdftotext is not used.
method.corpus: Every family whose MASTER_QUEUE.json state is COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN (150 at base 427afe413) plus ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set, ri_first_offender_felony-set, ri_first_offender_misdemeanor-set and ri_deferred_sentence-set. Every *.pdf under each family's fixtures/ directory, recursively, so the California per-form sub-directories and the multi-document fixtures (order/petition, crrlj-09-0100/0200, participant-guidance) are all opened, not only files named canonical.pdf and boundary.pdf.
method.routeKeySources: For each family: MASTER_QUEUE routeKeys, plus every obligation:... string in the family's production-field-map.json and source-receipt.json. Keys under 20 characters are ignored.

defectClasses.a_keyHardSplit: A line whose last whitespace-free token (10+ chars) is a proper prefix of one of the family's route keys, where the next drawn line (same page or the next page) opens on the remainder. Sub-kinds: MID_WORD (the cut falls inside a word of the key), BEFORE_OWN_SEPARATOR (the cut falls just before a : _ / . - so the next line opens on a stray delimiter). Both are counted as defects: both are what the char-by-char splitter produces and the shared splitter would not. AT_OWN_SEPARATOR (the line ends on the key's own separator) is the repaired splitter's break, is readable across, and is recorded but NOT counted.
defectClasses.b_routeKeyOnlyPage: A page on which every drawn line is either a route trailer line (starts 'Route:' or contains 'obligation:') or a continuation fragment of a key split from the line above. No heading, no prose.
defectClasses.c_keyBelowOrderSignature: On a page whose component (from reports/rendered-artifacts.json pageManifest) matches /order/i, a route-key line drawn below a signature or certification line. A signature/certification line is an execution line, not prose: it opens with JUDGE / DISTRICT JUDGE / JUDGE PRESIDING / JUSTICE / Justice / Judge / JUDICIAL OFFICER / SO ORDERED / ENTERED / Entered as an order / APPROVED AS TO FORM / Certification or attestation / Clerk distribution date / CLERK OF / SIGNATURE OF / Signature of, or carries a rule of 5+ dots or underscores together with judge|justice|clerk|certif|sign|entered|approved|attest. Parenthesised addressee lines are excluded. The same test on non-order pages is recorded as an observation only (keyBelowSignatureOnNonOrderPages_observation), because a petition's route footer under the petitioner's signature is the corpus convention the Captain has not ruled on.
defectClasses.d_markdownEmphasisPair: Added at the Captain's request during the run. FIX30's rule, replicated verbatim from scripts/rcap-custom-pleading/composed-page-markdown.mjs at d84991358 (read, not imported, not modified): a closed **...** or __...__ pair on the page text (lines joined on spaces), opening and closing on a non-space, not preceded/followed by its own delimiter character, and __ not inside a word. A run of three or more of the same character is not a pair. Each hit is localised to its drawn line and to the opening and closing delimiter's glyph x from the content stream, and tagged composerOrigin (x=72, 11pt) or not.

instrumentSource: // SCAN02 instrument. Read-only. Lives in the lane scratchpad, not in the tree;
// its full source is embedded in the committed JSON so the run is reproducible.
// Method (the verifiers' method, not SCAN01's): walk each page's composed
// content stream through the repo's own inflater (rcap-pdf-anchor-capture),
// reconstruct every drawn line in reading order, and match line text against
// the family's own route keys. No width band, no font metric is a criterion.
import { readdirSync, readFileSync, existsSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
// Class (d): FIX30's closed-emphasis-pair rule, replicated verbatim from

function markdownPairsIn(text) { const out = []; for (const d of DELIMITERS) for (const m of String(text ?? "").matchAll(pairPattern(d, "g"))) out.push({ delimiter: d.name, wraps: m[1], at: m.index, printed: m[0] }); return out.sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at); }
// A signature or certification line of an order: an execution line, not prose that mentions a clerk.

const SIG_HEAD = /^(JUDGE\b|DISTRICT JUDGE|JUDGE PRESIDING|JUSTICE\b|Justice \/ Judge|JUDICIAL OFFICER|SO ORDERED|ENTERED\b|Entered as an order|APPROVED AS TO FORM|Certification or attestation|Clerk distribution date|CLERK OF|SIGNATURE OF|Signature of)/;
async function font() { if (!FONT) { const d = await PDFDocument.create(); FONT = await d.embedFont(StandardFonts.TimesRoman); } return FONT; }
for (const q of adoption.adoption.qualifications) for (const f of q.families) adopted.set(f, { note: q.ownerNote.slice(0, 90), pins: (q.digestConditionRecordedPerFamily || {})[f] || null });

for (const r of registry.records) if (r.packetFamilyId) { if (!registryByFamily.has(r.packetFamilyId)) registryByFamily.set(r.packetFamilyId, []); registryByFamily.get(r.packetFamilyId).push({ recordId: r.recordId, routeId: r.routeId, revoked: !!(r.revocation && r.revocation.revoked), supersededBy: r.supersededBy ?? null }); }

const walk = (d) => { if (!existsSync(d)) return; for (const n of readdirSync(d).sort()) { const p = join(d, n); if (statSync(p).isDirectory()) walk(p); else if (n.toLowerCase().endsWith(".pdf")) out.push(p); } };
for (const a of r.artifacts || []) { const m = new Map(); for (const e of a.pageManifest || []) m.set(e.packetPage, e.component || e.documentId || null); out.set(a.file, m); }
function readMod(rel) { if (MOD.has(rel)) return MOD.get(rel); const p = join(ROOT, "scripts", rel); const s = existsSync(p) ? readFileSync(p, "latin1") : null; MOD.set(rel, s); return s; }
function lineOf(src, re) { const i = src.search(re); return i < 0 ? null : src.slice(0, i).split("\n").length; }
const seen = new Set(); const mods = [];
const src = readMod(rel); if (!src) return; mods.push({ rel, src });
for (const m of src.matchAll(/from "\.\/([A-Za-z0-9_./:\-]+\.mjs)"/g)) visit(m[1], depth + 1);

else if (priv) splitter = { kind: /\.split\(\/\(\?<=\[/.test(priv.src) ? "private separator-aware splitToken (inline FIX16/FIX17 repair, not yet on split-token.mjs)" : /for \(const (ch|char) of (tok|token)\)/.test(priv.src) ? "private char-by-char splitToken (pre-FIX16 fault)" : "private splitToken (variant unclassified)", inModule: `scripts/${priv.rel}:${lineOf(priv.src, /const splitToken = |function splitToken/)}` };
else splitter = { kind: "none found (no composer)", inModule: null };
const doc = await PDFDocument.load(readFileSync(abs), { updateMetadata: false, ignoreEncryption: true });
try { lines = groupIntoLines(extractTextItems(pages[i])).sort((a, b) => b.y - a.y); } catch { unreadablePages++; }

for (let j = 0; j < lines.length; j++) stream.push({ page: i + 1, idx: j, x: lines[j].x, y: lines[j].y, size: lines[j].size, text: lines[j].text.trim(), chars: lines[j].chars || [], keyLine: false, continuation: false });
perPage.push({ page: i + 1, from: start, to: stream.length, component: compMap ? compMap.get(i + 1) ?? null : null });
const lastTok = (t) => { const m = /(\S+)$/.exec(strip(t)); return m ? m[1] : ""; };
const firstTok = (t) => { const m = /^(\S+)/.exec(t); return m ? strip(m[1]).replace(/;$/, "") : ""; };
page: L.page, continuesOnPage: N.page, acrossPageBreak: N.page !== L.page,
fragmentA: { text: a, x: L.x, y: L.y, widthPt: widthOf(a), lineText: L.text },
fragmentB: { text: b, x: N.x, y: N.y, lineText: N.text },
classification: SEP_END.test(a) ? "key broken after its own separator: the repaired splitter's break, readable across, not counted as a defect"
: (/^[:_/.\-]/.test(b) ? "KEY_HARD_SPLIT: char-by-char cut landing just before a separator; the next line opens on a stray delimiter (the shared splitter would break after it)"
: "KEY_HARD_SPLIT_MID_WORD: char-by-char cut inside a word of the key")
const routeKeyOnlyPages = []; const keyBelowSignatureOnOrder = []; const keyBelowSignatureElsewhere = []; const markdownPairs = [];
// (d) FIX30's method on the page text (lines joined on spaces), then each hit localised to its drawn line and glyph x.
const raw = l.chars.length ? l.chars.map((c) => c.c).join("") : l.text;
const open = l.chars[m.at], close = l.chars[m.at + m.printed.length - 1];

loc = { y: l.y, xOpen: open ? open.x : l.x, xClose: close ? Number((close.x + close.w).toFixed(2)) : null, fontSize: l.size, composerOrigin: Math.abs(l.x - 72) < 0.01 && Math.abs(l.size - 11) < 0.01, lineText: l.text };

markdownPairs.push({ page: P.page, component: P.component, delimiter: hit.delimiter, printed: hit.printed, wraps: hit.wraps, ...(loc ?? { y: null, xOpen: null, xClose: null, note: "pair spans two drawn lines; coordinates not localised" }) });

if (lines.length && lines.every((l) => l.keyLine || l.continuation)) routeKeyOnlyPages.push({ page: P.page, component: P.component, lineCount: lines.length, printedAs: lines.map((l) => l.text), topY: lines[0].y });
const isOrder = P.component ? /order/i.test(P.component) : lines.some((l) => /Justice \/ Judge|JUDICIAL OFFICER|SO ORDERED|Entered as an order/.test(l.text));
const sigAbove = lines.filter((l) => l.y > k.y && !l.keyLine && isSigLine(l.text));

const rec = { page: P.page, component: P.component, routeLine: { text: k.text, x: k.x, y: k.y }, signatureOrCertificationLine: { text: nearest.text, y: nearest.y }, gapPt: Number((nearest.y - k.y).toFixed(1)) };

return { pageCount: pages.length, unreadablePages, lineCount: stream.length, keyLinesPrinted: stream.filter((l) => l.keyLine).length, splits, routeKeyOnlyPages, keyBelowSignatureOnOrder, keyBelowSignatureElsewhere, markdownPairs };

const r = await scanPdf(abs, keys, comps.get(rel) ?? null);
pages += r.pageCount; unreadable += r.unreadablePages; keyLines += r.keyLinesPrinted;
rko += r.routeKeyOnlyPages.length; below += r.keyBelowSignatureOnOrder.length; belowElse += r.keyBelowSignatureElsewhere.length; md += r.markdownPairs.length;
} catch (e) { fixtures[rel] = { role: roleOf(rel), unreadable: true, reason: String(e && e.message || e) }; }
const defective = midToken + rko + below + md > 0;

whyScan01Missed.theShortAnswer: It did not miss them. SCAN01's committed sweep (data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/scan01/composed-pdf-text-integrity-sweep.json, captured at Captain tip 77848f5a) lists ms-misd-1st-set with 10 hard_split_token defects on canonical pages 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and the same five boundary pages, ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set with 16 hard splits and 2 fragment pages, ri_first_offender_felony-set with 8 and 4, ri_first_offender_misdemeanor-set with 16, and ri_deferred_sentence-set with 4 route_key_only_page. Its findings.familiesAffected is 40, not 0. No SCAN01 artifact in the tree reports zero affected families; the only zeros are the positive control (hard splits after FIX16/FIX17 on the four already-repaired families) and FIX21's per-cohort inertness counts.

whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.gap: NO JOIN TO THE PROVEN STATE. SCAN01 is laneKind 'measurement': 'No verdict is issued and no route is opened or closed.' The factory state machine reads verdicts only from a lane's rows.json, and SCAN01 writes none. Its 40-family worklist was consumed by FIX21/FIX23 for the Georgia/Kentucky/Oklahoma/Washington cohorts and never dispatched for rcap-custom-pleading/composed-family-host.mjs (which SCAN01 itself named as carrying ms-misd-1st-set and ms-nonconv-set) or for build-census-v1-ri_decriminalized-set.mjs (which it named as carrying the four Rhode Island families). A proven family with a SCAN01 hit therefore stayed proven.
whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.evidence: sweep.cohorts.sharedComposerHosts[0] = rcap-custom-pleading/composed-family-host.mjs, familiesAffected 3 incl. ms-misd-1st-set; sharedComposerHosts[3] = build-census-v1-ri_decriminalized-set.mjs, familiesAffected 4 (all four RI). MASTER_QUEUE at 427afe413 still carries ms-misd-1st-set as COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN with vf02's base-less PASS.

whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.gap: THE RECORD SAYS scan01SawIt:false, AND THAT IS WRONG. The vf06 row for ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set states the defect is not seen 'by the corpus SCAN01 sweep, which classifies this family as official-pdf-fill and does not visit it', and MASTER_QUEUE carries scan01SawIt:false for it. The sweep does classify it official-pdf-fill AND measured it: fixturesRead 2, composedPages 18, tokensMeasured 6105, hard_split_token 16, fragment_page 2, with the exact fragments '...-affidav' / 'it' and '...-certif' / 'ied-copies'. Component kind is a label in SCAN01's output, not an enumeration filter: familyDirs() walks every census-v1 family directory and pdfsUnder() every PDF under fixtures/, regardless of kind.
whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.evidence: sweep.findings.perFamily entry for ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set; vf06/rows.json last row; MASTER_QUEUE.json 'scan01SawIt': false.

whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.gap: MEASUREMENT GAP 1: route-key-only pages that carry a split key are reported as fragment_page, not route_key_only_page. SCAN01's isTrailerish() accepts a line only if it starts 'Route: ' or is a single whitespace-free token containing ':'. The continuation lines the char-by-char splitter leaves behind, 'it ;' (contains a space) and 'ied-copies' (no colon), fail both tests, so page 8 of ri_multiple_misdemeanors-set and the RI first-offender pages are counted under B_page_content/fragment_page (still a defect class, but the wrong name for a page that is nothing but the route key). ri_deferred_sentence-set, whose 459.74pt key is never split, is the only RI family SCAN01 names route_key_only_page. Any reader who filtered the sweep on route_key_only_page alone would see one RI family, not four.
whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.evidence: scripts/rcap-scan01-composed-pdf-text-integrity.mjs isTrailerish; sweep perFamily defectCountsByKind for the four RI families.

whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.gap: MEASUREMENT GAP 2: no class for a route key printed below an order's signature or certification line. SCAN01 has classes A (hard split), B (page content), C (block integrity), D (census). The verifiers' third finding, the internal identifier sitting under the clerk's certification on the RI proposed order and under the judicial officer / APPROVED AS TO FORM block on the Mississippi proposed order, is not something SCAN01 measures at all. SCAN02 measures it as class c.
whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.evidence: Class list in the script header; vf06 row: 'Page 6 is the proposed order, so the internal identifiers appear directly beneath the clerk's certification line'.

whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.gap: THE SWEEP IS A SNAPSHOT AND ONE PROVEN FAMILY REGRESSED AFTER IT. az_wrongful_arrest_clearance-set measured clean at 77848f5a (widest token 277.07pt). It was rebuilt at e3e344d88 ('fix(az): add notarization guidance') and 64f2dbb8e, and its current bytes carry the key cut '...-a-wrongful-arrest' / '-under-13-4051' on pages 2 and 4 of both fixtures. SCAN01 run today on that family reports 4 hard_split_token; the committed sweep still says clean. No re-sweep gate runs when a family is rebuilt.
whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.evidence: sweep.familiesMeasuredAndClean entry for az_wrongful_arrest_clearance-set (widestTokenPt 277.07); SCAN01_ONLY=az-wrongful-arrest-clearance run at 427afe413 -> 4 defects; git log on the fixture.

whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.gap: BAND-FLOOR BLIND SPOT (latent, no instance in this corpus). SCAN01's class A requires the prefix fragment to measure inside (457.6, 468]pt, which is only guaranteed for a splitter that emits the maximal prefix that fits. The Indiana/Louisiana variant SCAN01 itself describes ('pushes the oversized chunk out whole and starts the next piece fresh') and any future splitter that breaks early would put fragments under the floor. Key matching has no floor: it flags the fragment because it IS a prefix of the key.
whereTheContradictionActuallyComesFrom.evidence: SCAN01 header comment and hardSplitTest.band; fix21 return line 46.

whyScan01Missed.inTwoSentences: SCAN01's sweep did open and did flag all five families (10 hard splits on ms-misd-1st-set, 16/8/16 on the three split Rhode Island families, 4 route-key-only pages on ri_deferred_sentence-set), but it is a verdict-less measurement whose worklist was never joined to the COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN state and was dispatched only for four cohorts, so the composed-family-host and ri_decriminalized-set hosts were never repaired and the record's 'scan01SawIt: false' is simply wrong. Two instrument gaps compound it: split-key trailer pages are misnamed fragment_page instead of route_key_only_page, there is no class for a key under an order's signature line, and the sweep is a stale snapshot (Arizona regressed after it).

scan01SweepCrossCheck.agreement: Every family SCAN01's sweep lists with hard_split_token in this corpus is found by SCAN02 with the identical instance count; SCAN02 additionally finds az_wrongful_arrest_clearance-set (rebuilt after the sweep). Families SCAN01 listed only for fragment_page/thin_page/orphaned_execution_block (e.g. ga-* after FIX21/FIX23, wy_fel_1502-set, tx_exp_acquittal-set) show no hard split here; where SCAN02 still lists them it is for class b or c.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: No verdict. The state of any family is unchanged by this file; a repair lane and an independent verifier act on it.
A family listed INSPECTED_NO_DEFECT is clean on classes a-d only; nothing here speaks to legal correctness, source fidelity, visual review or raster state.

Keys broken after their own separator (rcap-ok, rcap-tn, rcap-wa, la-977) are the repaired splitter's behaviour and are not counted; they are recorded per family so a future rule can be applied without re-measuring.
